title:
A "call" represents calling a function or lambda value with a set of argument values passed in the regular way.
This is useful when the function is computed, but the arguments are known at code-generation time.

For example:
```js
let op = this.binaryOpImpl();
return op.call(this, left, right);
```
Here we have the function to call as an expression, but we know the arguments are code-generation time so we
pass them explicitly.

In Python there is no special form:
```py
op = this.binaryOpImpl()
op(this, left, right)
```

In Java, this only makes sense for lambdas. Also, lambdas have various different method names, such as "apply",
"accept", "get" and "test".

@see Code.Invocation
@see Code.Apply
